Plot each profile's probability of one response category on every categorical or ordinal indicator

Source: R/plot-named.R
plot_responses.Rd

plot_responses() plots how likely each profile (class) is to give one response category. There is one line per profile, joining the probability of the chosen category on every categorical or ordinal indicator, on a 0 to 1 axis. The categorical indicators carry 95% intervals, formed on the logit scale, when the fit has standard errors.

Usage

plot_responses(
  x,
  category = "last",
  intervals = TRUE,
  labels = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A profile, class or transition fit with categorical or ordinal indicators: from lca(), multilca(), lpa() or multilpa() (with or without membership covariates), or from lta() with categorical indicators. An lta() fit of class multilpa_lta (ordinal or count indicators, covariates, weights, a stayer class, second-order or occasion-specific transitions, occasion-specific measurement) is not drawn: read its probabilities with get_results(x, "responses") or get_results(x, "ordinal").

category

Which category's probability is drawn:

  • "last" (default): the last category of each indicator, which for a no/yes indicator is the probability of "yes";

  • "first": the first category of each indicator;

  • one category label (such as "yes") or one whole-number position (such as 2), which every indicator must have.

intervals

TRUE (default) draws the 95% intervals of parameter_inference(); a fit that has no standard errors is drawn without them, and the subtitle says why. A probability estimated at 0 or 1 is held there and has no interval. FALSE draws no intervals and does not compute them.

labels

TRUE (default) writes each profile's name at the end of its line; FALSE uses a legend instead.

data

The data frame the model was fitted to, used only to compute the intervals. NULL (default) uses the data stored in the fit.

main, subtitle

Title and subtitle of the plot, each one string; NULL (default) keeps the view's own.

Value

A ggplot object, which draws the plot when printed. Conditions raised:

  • latents_no_categorical: a profile, class or transition fit without categorical or ordinal indicators;

  • latents_unknown_category: category is not a category of every indicator;

  • latents_nothing_to_plot: a model of another family, which has no response view; the message names the plot functions that apply;

  • latents_not_a_fit: x is not a fitted model.

See also

plot_profiles() for continuous indicators; plot_heatmap() for every category at once.

Examples

fit <- lca(student_esm, c("time_with_friends", "on_social_media", "sports"),
           n_classes = 2, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
plot_responses(fit)

plot_responses(fit, category = "no")
